newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian sorghum market waits on harvest.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian sorghum market waits on harvest.

text.p: Australian domestic demand remained quiet for old and new crop sorghum over the past weelk with little tonnage traded, Queensland grain cooperative Grainco said in its weekly report.
Most end-users appeared to have sufficient cover through to new crop barley and were waiting to see what the winter harvest brought before committing themselves, it said.
Grainco said new crop sorghum values finished the past week at A$168.00 a tonne, delivered port, down slightly on the week.
Feed barley values were a little lower over the past week to A$168 a tonne delivered Brisbane.

While the international market saw some action over the past week with purchases by Saudi Arabia and Canadian barley reportedly trading into Japan, the Australian domestic market remained quiet, Grainco said.
The export market was likely to find support at around US$145 a tonne on the Saudi business, it said.
International malting barley remains quiet with world production looking healthy.
The cottonseed market was also quiet in the past week, it said.

Domestic sunflower values were unchanged over the past week with new crop finishing at A$370 a tonne delivered Brisbane, Moree and central Queensland, and at around A$325-A$330 a tonne delivered depot.
New crop soybeans were unchanged at A$405 a tonne, while canola fell by A$2 a tonne to A$392 a tonne November/December delivery.
